title: GPU subnetting and adaptive quota rebalance for noisy-neighbor containment
creator: Priya Reddy
description:
Problem: Customers on Redwood Dedicated occasionally experience severe latency and tail spikes when a co-located tenant runs bursty inference patterns (long context, many small requests, or heavy KV-cache churn). Current hard-slice and token-bucket mechanisms blunt the effect but cause underutilization or abrupt evictions that break long-running sessions.

Goal: Implement an isolation model that combines lightweight GPU 'subnets' (logical pool carving), predictive noisy-neighbor detection, and an adaptive quota rebalance controller. The system should: (1) confine noisy workloads into bounded subnets when possible, (2) proactively rebalance soft quotas across subnets to preserve throughput contracts, and (3) perform graceful soft-evictions/minimal-impact throttling for harmful workloads while preserving SLA guarantees for committed capacity holders.

Scope: Dedicated GPU pools only (not hosted API). Includes control-plane controllers for allocation decisions, runtime agents on pod sidecars for real-time telemetry and KV-cache pressure signals, and Console UI telemetry surfaces for per-subnet health and rebalance actions. Not in scope: full rework of admission controller; initial iteration will extend existing allocator and quota services.
acceptance_criteria: Define GPU subnet abstraction that can be applied to existing capacity pools without node-level reconfiguration
Telemetry pipeline surfaces per-subnet request rate, active KV cache size, LRU churn, per-tenant token usage, and P95/P99 latency
Controller can detect noisy behavior with precision >= 85% on historical test traces and trigger mitigations
Soft-rebalance moves up to 20% of soft quota from low-util subnets to high-demand subnets without violating hard commitments
Mitigation actions (rate-limit, lane-quarantine, graceful-evict) have documented rollback and safety checks; no disruption to pinned dedicated reservations
E2E test that simulates mixed workloads (committed tenants + bursty tenants) demonstrates <10% P90 degradation for committed tenants during peak rebalance
design_notes: GPU subnet = logical label + soft/hard quota; affinity rules map tenant contracts to subnet labels
Realtime noisy-detection uses a sliding histogram of per-tenant token emission rate, KV cache miss ratio, and kernel queue length to compute a noise-score
Adaptive rebalance uses a PID-inspired controller with cooldown windows and hysteresis to avoid oscillation
Soft-eviction preserves partial KV cache checkpoints and signals client SDKs with Retry-After and graceful pause hooks
Controller records every rebalance decision as an immutable event for audit and post-incident analysis
implementation_plan: 1) Add subnet metadata to pool API and extend allocator to place new reservations into subnets
2) Ship sidecar telemetry agent (go) that emits KV cache metrics + per-request kernel queue counters to our metrics pipeline
3) Build noise-detection microservice and create a simulation harness to tune thresholds against replay traces
4) Implement adaptive-rebalance controller in control-plane with opt-in feature flag for pilot customers
5) Add Console views: subnet map, recent rebalance events, and tenant-level impact projections
6) Run canary with two enterprise customers on dedicated capacity, observe telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Oscillations from naive rebalance -> Mitigation: hysteresis + rate limit rebalance actions; simulation tests
Risk: Misclassification of latency spikes as noisy neighbor -> Mitigation: ensemble detector (histograms + change point + model-score) and reversible actions
Risk: Impact on pinned reservations -> Mitigation: hard quotas and strict reservation precedence; controller cannot touch hard-committed units
Risk: Increased control-plane load -> Mitigation: batch decisions and backoff; telemetry sampling at 1s->5s in high-volume pools
metrics_to_track: Per-subnet utilization and soft quota variance
Number of rebalance events per-day and mean time to stabilize
False positive rate of noisy-detection on replay dataset
Fraction of requests receiving graceful-eviction vs hard-eviction
testing_plan: Unit tests for telemetry agent and noise-score computation
Replay simulation using production traces (sanitized) with labelled noisy events
Chaos test: inject noisy process that sporadically allocates long-context workloads and verify containment
Canary rollout to two customers with manual kill-switch in console
Load test to measure control-plane CPU/memory impact at fleet scale
